lead.title: 87GB Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on CPU-only at 8 tokens/s
lead.summary: An r/LocalLLaMA benchmark shoved the 87.2 GiB Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF through llama.cpp on a CPU-only box)Skip sustaining roughly 8.34 tok/s decode, and about 109 tok/s once the GPU layer sits fully in VRAM. Putting the embedding table on GPU delivered a large decode boost at long context, illustrating the architecture's design tradeoffs for low-memory local runs.

top_stories.title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: first open-weight Qwen3.6 variant, Apache 2.0 sparse MoE
top_stories.summary: Alibaba released Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a 35B-total/~3B-active multimodal sparse MoE focused on agentic coding with a 'thinking preservation' feature. Same-day support across vLLM, SGLang, Ollama and Unsloth GGUFs (~22-23GB RAM) makes it immediately usable locally.

top_stories.title: BenchMIRT audits what LLM benchmarks actually measure
top_stories.summary: AI2's Olmo team released BenchMIRT, a multidimensional Item Response Theory method for auditing benchmarks at question level across 100 open-weight LLMs and 16 benchmarks. It recovered safety and general reasoning as the dominant measured capabilities and can rank the most informative questions.

top_stories.title: Qualcomm and HUMAIN unveil Horizon Ultra AI PC at LEAP 2026
top_stories.summary: The Horizon Ultra runs on Snapdragon X2 Elite (18-core Oryon CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) and runs AI models on-device with optional cloud extension. Enterprise availability starts September 20, 2026 on Windows, with a HUMAIN OS variant planned for 2027.

top_stories.title: Superagent: a local home for your coding agent on Mac
top_stories.summary: A free, MIT-licensed Mac app where a local coding agent lives: it drives a real browser signed in as you, streams a live iPhone simulator, and keeps chats across restarts, all on-device with no account and no telemetry. Works with Claude Code, with Codex and Antigravity coming.

items.title: A mathematical theory of reusable neural bases for network compression
items.summary: Proposes the Linear Reusable Neural Bases Architecture (LRNBA), a framework to improve parameter efficiency and mitigate the memory cost bottleneck in large-model training and inference.

items.title: Breaking structural identity: personalized federated LoRA under rank heterogeneity
items.summary: Addresses resource-efficient federated fine-tuning of LLMs with LoRA under heterogeneous rank budgets across privacy-sensitive, distributed clients.

items.title: Fountain: open-source conversational API that gives your app a computer
items.summary: A self-hosted AGPL engine that spins up a sandboxed coding agent with repos, tools and credentials from a single prompt. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode runtimes, attaches MCP servers, and keeps all conversations in your own Postgres.

items.title: Markdown Gatekeeper: local-first authority layer for agent-facing Markdown
items.summary: A local-first CLI that keeps ordinary Markdown and Git but enforces one rule: a document doesn't become current authority just because an agent calls it authoritative. Works with Claude Code and Codex via native Skills and hooks, no cloud service and no MCP dependency.
